meta.title: WOAH PVS Pathway Good Practices
meta.source: The PVS (Performance of Veterinary Services) Pathway is the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) programme that helps Members assess and improve their Veterinary Services against WOAH international standards. Steps: orientation, PVS Evaluation, planning (PVS Gap Analysis, strategic planning support), and targeted support (such as One Health integration, the Veterinary Legislation Support Programme, sustainable laboratories and workforce development), with PVS Follow-up missions. WOAH counted 448 PVS activities in 2006 to 2021. The PVS Tool has 45 critical competencies (CCs) in four fundamental components; each CC receives a level of advancement from 1 to 5.

meta.itemsLabel: Critical competencies in this topic (WOAH wording)
meta.note: The list of competencies follows a WOAH slide set from 2019 (the A and B parts are counted separately to reach 45); later editions of the PVS Tool may word things differently. The crosswalk to JEE, SPAR and PHEPA is our own and is not official. WOAH PVS reports are often confidential to the Member unless it publishes them.
meta.groupsNote: Fundamental components of the PVS Tool

topics.group: I. Human, physical and financial resources
topics.title: Staffing, competence and continuing education
topics.what: Whether the Veterinary Services have enough qualified veterinarians and paraprofessionals, trained to the right level and kept up to date.
items: Staffing: veterinary and other professionals (university qualified) / veterinary paraprofessionals
Competency and education of veterinarians / veterinary paraprofessionals

topics.group: I. Human, physical and financial resources
topics.title: Independence, planning and coordination
topics.what: Technical independence of the Veterinary Services, planning and management of policies and programmes, and internal and external coordination (including One Health).
items: Planning, sustainability and management of policies and programmes
Coordination capability: internal (chain of command) / external (including the One Health approach)

topics.group: I. Human, physical and financial resources
topics.title: Physical resources and funding
topics.what: Buildings, equipment and capital investment, operational funding and emergency funding.

topics.title: Veterinary laboratories
topics.what: Access to laboratory diagnosis, whether the national laboratory system is suitable, and laboratory quality management.
items: Suitability of the national laboratory system

topics.title: Risk analysis, surveillance and early detection
topics.what: Risk analysis and epidemiology, passive surveillance and outbreak investigation, and active surveillance and monitoring.
items: Surveillance and early detection: passive surveillance, early detection and epidemiological outbreak investigation
Surveillance and early detection: active surveillance and monitoring

topics.title: Emergency response, disease control and borders
topics.what: Quarantine and border security, emergency preparedness and response, and disease prevention, control and eradication.

topics.title: Food of animal origin, residues and feed
topics.what: Inspection and authorisation of food establishments, ante- and post-mortem inspection, residue testing and animal feed safety.
items: Regulation, inspection, authorisation and supervision of establishments for production and processing of food of animal origin

topics.title: Veterinary medicines and AMR
topics.what: Control of veterinary medicines and biologicals, and antimicrobial resistance and antimicrobial use.

topics.title: Identification, traceability and animal welfare
topics.what: Identification and movement control of animals and premises, traceability of animal products, and animal welfare.
items: Premises, herd, batch and animal identification, tracing and movement control
Identification, traceability and control of products of animal origin

topics.title: Communication and consultation
topics.what: Communication, consultation with stakeholders, and participation of producers in joint programmes.
items: Participation of producers and other stakeholders in joint programmes

topics.title: International role, delegation and the profession
topics.what: Official representation and international collaboration, accreditation and delegation, regulation of the profession, and veterinary clinical services.
items: Regulation of the profession by the Veterinary Statutory Body

topics.title: Veterinary legislation
topics.what: Legal quality and coverage of veterinary legislation, and how well it is implemented and complied with.
items: Veterinary legislation: legal quality and coverage

topics.title: Trade standards, certification and zoning
topics.what: International harmonisation, certification, equivalence agreements, transparency, zoning and compartmentalisation.
items: Equivalence and other types of sanitary agreements

topics.title: One Health bridge: IHR-PVS workshops and JEE
topics.what: JEE is the human-health counterpart of the PVS Evaluation. IHR-PVS National Bridging Workshops (NBWs) put the two reports side by side so human and animal health can agree a joint roadmap.
items: Three-day workshop with about 60 to 90 people from human and animal health; other sectors such as environment, wildlife, media and police often join.
After a JEE and before a national action plan; a recent PVS Evaluation or Follow-up is preferred.
A diagnosis of strengths and weaknesses across 16 joint technical areas and a joint roadmap agreed by prioritisation vote.
